Build a dedicated GAME SERVER control panel for Nxeon — the biggest gap in the game vertical. Work EXCLUSIVELY in /opt/nxeon-wt-gamepanel (branch feature/gap-gamepanel). node_modules symlinked. Do NOT run build/prisma commands — code only. Do NOT touch order/renewal/billing money files.

CONTEXT: Game servers are marketed heavily (Minecraft/Rust/Valheim/Palworld/CS2/Terraria under app/(marketing)/), but management is just a static config-file editor — lib/game-config.ts + lib/actions-game-config.ts (getGameConfig/saveGameConfig) riding on the generic VPS noVNC console. Missing vs Pterodactyl/Nitrado: a live console, RCON commands, scheduled restarts, world/save management, one-click mod/plugin install.

STUDY FIRST: how game servers run — lib/games.ts (the 6 game families + how each is installed/run), worker/game-update.ts (how the worker SSHes into the game VM — sshpass/execFile array args, and note it scrubs the root password from errors), lib/actions-gameplans.ts, the Server model (gamePlanId), components/customer/GameSettings.tsx / GameDeploy.tsx / GameAutoUpdate.tsx, and how the game process is managed (systemd unit? screen/tmux? pm2?). Understand the run model before adding control features.

BUILD a game control panel (a "Manage" tab for a game server) with a SECURE, MVP-scoped feature set — all operating on the customer's OWN game VM over the platform's existing SSH (reuse worker/game-update.ts's connection pattern; validate every input; never shell-inject; keep the root password out of any error surfaced to the customer):
1. **Server power/lifecycle for the game process**: start / stop / restart the game service (systemctl or the equivalent the install uses) — distinct from the VM power.
2. **Live console / logs**: stream recent game-server logs to the panel (tail the log/journal over SSH), with an input box to send a console/RCON command to the running server. For games with RCON (Minecraft, Rust, CS2, Palworld, Valheim), wire RCON (read the server's RCON port/password from its config); for others, send to the process stdin/console if feasible, else disable with a note. Validate/escape all command input.
3. **Scheduled restarts**: let the customer schedule automatic restarts (e.g. daily at HH:MM) — persist a schedule (schema: a GameSchedule or reuse a cron-like table) and have a worker sweep execute it; announce to players via RCON before restart if supported.
4. **World/save management**: list save/world files, download a backup of the world, and (careful) restore/upload — scoped to the game's data dir, path-validated (no traversal). Reuse the existing backup machinery if a game backup exists.
5. **Player list** (where RCON supports it): show connected players; kick/ban via RCON.
(One-click mod/plugin install is a nice-to-have — include a stub/placeholder or a simple "upload a mod jar/pak to the mods dir" if time; flag if deferred.)

Schema: add whatever's needed (e.g. GameSchedule, or fields on Server for RCON/scheduled-restart) — additive, cascade on Server delete. Server actions ownership-guarded (caller owns the game server). Worker executes over SSH with validated inputs only.

SECURITY: it's the customer's own VM, but validate/escape every RCON command, filename, schedule field, and port before it reaches a shell/RCON; never interpolate raw strings into a shell command (execFile array args, like worker/game-update.ts); never surface node/root credentials.

DELIVER an MVP (power + live console/RCON + scheduled restarts + world list/backup at minimum; player list if RCON is wired), then commit `git add -A && git commit -m "feat: game server control panel (console/RCON, power, scheduled restarts, world mgmt)"` (trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>), `git push -u origin feature/gap-gamepanel`. REPORT (factual, detailed): schema added, each feature + how it executes over SSH, how RCON creds are read + commands validated, the anti-injection handling, per-game coverage (which of the 6 support RCON), and what's deferred. Don't claim tested.

455	 * Resolve the game family for a server, preferring the game plan's family and
456	 * falling back to the OS template's family. Returns the family string ONLY if a

458	 */
459	export function familyFor(server: ServerLike | null | undefined): string | null {
460	  if (!server) return null;
461	  const fam = server.gamePlan?.gameFamily ?? server.osTemplate?.family ?? null;
462	  if (fam && GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS[fam]) return fam;
463	  return null;

466	/** The customization schema for a family, or null. */
467	export function schemaFor(family: string | null | undefined): FamilySchema | null {
468	  if (!family) return null;
469	  return GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS[family] ?? null;
470	}

472	/** True if `variant` is a valid variant id for `family`. */
473	export function isValidVariant(family: string, variant: string): boolean {
474	  const s = GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS[family];
475	  return !!s && s.variants.some((v) => v.id === variant);
476	}

478	export type ValidateResult =
479	  | { ok: true; values: Record<string, string | number | boolean> }
480	  | { ok: false; error: string };
481	
482	/**
483	 * Validate & coerce a settings object against a family's field schema. Unknown
484	 * keys are dropped; missing keys fall back to the field default. Returns a clean,
485	 * fully-populated values object ready to persist to `Server.gameConfig`.
486	 */
487	export function validateConfig(
488	  family: string,
489	  values: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined
490	): ValidateResult {
491	  const schema = GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS[family];
492	  if (!schema) return { ok: false, error: `Unknown game family "${family}".` };
493	
494	  const input = values ?? {};
495	  const out: Record<string, string | number | boolean> = {};
496	
497	  for (const field of schema.fields) {
498	    const raw = input[field.key];
499	    const provided = raw !== undefined && raw !== null;
500	
501	    switch (field.type) {
502	      case "bool": {
503	        out[field.key] = provided ? raw === true || raw === "true" || raw === "on" : (field.default as boolean);
504	        break;
505	      }
506	      case "int": {
507	        let n = provided ? Number(raw) : (field.default as number);
508	        if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} must be a number.` };
509	        n = Math.trunc(n);
510	        if (field.min !== undefined && n < field.min)
511	          return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} must be at least ${field.min}.` };
512	        if (field.max !== undefined && n > field.max)
513	          return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} must be at most ${field.max}.` };
514	        out[field.key] = n;
515	        break;
516	      }
517	      case "enum": {
518	        const v = provided ? String(raw) : String(field.default);
519	        if (!field.options?.some((o) => o.value === v))
520	          return { ok: false, error: `Invalid value for ${field.label}.` };
521	        out[field.key] = v;
522	        break;
523	      }
524	      case "string": {
525	        const v = provided ? String(raw) : String(field.default);
526	        if (v.length > 256) return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} is too long (max 256 chars).` };
527	        // CONFIG INJECTION: these values are written verbatim into LINE-ORIENTED
528	        // files on the customer's VM by worker/game-config.ts —
529	        // `server.properties` (`motd=<value>`), Rust's `server.cfg`
530	        // (`server.hostname "<value>"`) and Valheim's launch-args file. A newline
531	        // therefore does not set one option, it appends arbitrary further
532	        // options: a motd of "hi\nenable-rcon=true\nrcon.password=x" turns RCON
533	        // on with a chosen password, and that password is then read back out of
534	        // the same file and interpolated into an `mcrcon` command line.
535	        // `enum`/`int`/`bool` are constrained by their own branches; `string` was
536	        // the only field type with no allowlist at all, so it is checked here —
537	        // at the one point every caller (UI, server action and worker re-validation)
538	        // already goes through.
539	        // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
540	        if (/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(v)) {
541	          return {
542	            ok: false,
543	            error: `${field.label} may not contain line breaks or control characters.`,
544	          };
545	        }
546	        out[field.key] = v;
547	        break;
548	      }
549	    }
550	  }
551	
552	  return { ok: true, values: out };
553	}

For RCON specifically, I'm weighing whether to use an existing Node library or implement the Source RCON protocol directly. Since the RCON port is typically bound to localhost on the game VM, the most reliable approach for an MVP is to mirror the existing pattern: run an RCON CLI tool like mcrcon over SSH on the remote host itself, rather than trying to connect directly from the worker to the VM's RCON port.

Actually, there's a cleaner option: implement a minimal Source RCON client in TypeScript within the worker and use SSH port forwarding via ssh2's `forwardOut` method to tunnel the TCP connection through the existing authenticated SSH session. This way I can communicate with the game's RCON server at 127.0.0.1 on the VM without needing extra tools installed, exposing ports, or transmitting credentials outside the server.

The Source RCON protocol is straightforward—packets consist of a little-endian length prefix, an ID, a type field, a null-terminated string body, and a trailing null byte. Authentication uses type 3 with the password, and the server responds with type 2 (success returns the request ID, failure returns -1). Commands use type 2 and get a type 0 response.

Now I'm checking which games actually support this protocol and how they implement RCON—Minecraft uses Source RCON, CS2 uses it too, but Rust uses WebSocket RCON instead, and Valheim doesn't have built-in RCON support at all.

Looking at the practical reality: Minecraft, CS2, and Palworld can all be controlled via Source-style RCON, though Palworld's response handling is a bit quirky. Rust requires WebSocket RCON, and Terraria only has stdin console in vanilla (though TShock adds a REST server). So for a unified approach, I'm focusing on the three games that genuinely support Source RCON.

For the MVP, I'll build a solid Source RCON client that tunnels through SSH port forwarding and works across Minecraft, CS2, and Palworld. Rust's WebSocket RCON is more complex—it needs HTTP upgrade handshakes and WebSocket framing over the forwarded connection—so I'll either implement it properly or mark it as deferred with a clear note about what's needed.

Valheim and Terraria don't have native RCON, so I'll document that console input isn't available for those games. /**
 * A customer-defined automatic action on a GAME server — MVP: a daily restart at
 * a fixed UTC time. The worker sweep (worker/game-control.ts gameScheduleSweep)
 * enqueues a GAME_POWER restart when `nextRunAt` falls due, optionally announcing

 * `nextRunAt` is the single source of truth the sweep selects on; it is (re)computed

 * UTC in the MVP (the UI states this) — no per-customer timezone yet.
 */
model GameSchedule {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  serverId  String
  server    Server   @relation(fields: [serverId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  // "restart" is the only kind today; the column exists so start/stop/backup

  announce  Boolean  @default(true)
  lastRunAt DateTime?
  nextRunAt DateTime?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  @@index([enabled, nextRunAt])
  @@index([serverId])
}

  **Source RCON** to `127.0.0.1:<rcon port>` on the VM **through the SSH connection** (`conn.forwardOut`),

  arg. `lib/game-control.ts` (`sourceRcon`, `runRcon`, `readRconCreds`).
- **Players** — RCON list + kick/ban (player ids allowlisted before templating into an RCON verb).
- **Worlds & backups** — list save entries with sizes; `GAME_BACKUP` job tars the world dir into
  `/var/backups/nxeon-game/<family>-<ts>.tar.gz`, downloaded through the existing `/api/files` route.

  `gameScheduleSweep()` (~60 s) enqueues a `GAME_POWER` restart when a row falls due and advances
  `nextRunAt`.

**Per-game RCON coverage.** Source RCON is wired for **Minecraft, CS2, Palworld** (creds read from
`server.properties` / `server.cfg` / `PalWorldSettings.ini`). **Rust** uses WebSocket RCON — deferred;

## Game Server Control Panel — MVP delivered

Branch `feature/gap-gamepanel` pushed to origin (commit `d058a52`). Built entirely in `/opt/nxeon-wt-gamepanel`, code-only (no build/prisma run). Not tested against a live VM.

### Schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`, additive)
- `JobType` += `GAME_POWER` (start/stop/restart the game *service*) and `GAME_BACKUP` (world archive).
- New model `GameSchedule` (id, serverId→Server **cascade on delete**, kind, hour, minute, enabled, announce, lastRunAt, nextRunAt, timestamps; indexed on `[enabled,nextRunAt]` and `[serverId]`) + `Server.gameSchedules GameSchedule[]`.

### Files
- `lib/game-control.ts` — plain module (no `"use server"`): per-family `GAME_CONTROL` spec table, all validators, Source-RCON client, SSH-tunnel transport, inline SSH readers. Imported by both worker and actions.
- `lib/actions-game-control.ts` — `"use server"` actions (ownership-guarded, rate-limited, SANDBOX-synthetic).
- `worker/game-control.ts` — `gamePower`, `gameBackup`, `gameScheduleSweep`; wired into `worker/index.ts` (handlers map + a ~60s sweep timer).
- `components/customer/game/GameManage.tsx` + a "Manage" tab injected into `ServerTabs` (game servers only) and the server detail page.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` updated (job-type table, sweep table, new feature chapter).

### Features & how each executes over SSH
All operate on the customer's **own** game VM via the existing `withServerSsh` (host/port/root-password derived exactly like `lib/sftp.ts`). SANDBOX returns synthetic data; real path guarded by `!SANDBOX` + `status===RUNNING`.
1. **Power** — `GAME_POWER` job. Worker resolves the systemd unit from compile-time family hints (falls back to `systemctl list-units | grep -i <family>`), runs `systemctl start|stop|restart`, and checks the real exit code via `NXGP:` markers (a clean SSH exit alone is never treated as success — same discipline as `worker/game-update.ts`).
2. **Live console/logs + RCON** — inline reads: `journalctl -u <unit> -n N` with a `*.log` fallback under the data roots. Command box speaks **Source RCON** to `127.0.0.1:<rconport>` **through the SSH connection** via `conn.forwardOut` (RCON port never exposed off-box).
3. **Scheduled restarts** — `GameSchedule` CRUD; `gameScheduleSweep()` selects due rows (`nextRunAt<=now`), enqueues a `GAME_POWER` restart with announce, advances `nextRunAt` to next day. Times are UTC (UI states this).
4. **World/save management** — inline listing (`du -sb` of top-level entries in the located data dir); `GAME_BACKUP` job tars the dir into `/var/backups/nxeon-game/<family>-<ts>.tar.gz`; existing backups listed with download links through the existing `/api/files/[serverId]` route.
5. **Player list** — RCON `list`/`ShowPlayers`/`status`; kick/ban build a command from an allowlisted player id.

### RCON creds + validation / anti-injection
- **Creds** read from each game's own config over SSH (`server.properties` → enable-rcon/rcon.password/rcon.port; CS2 `server.cfg` → rcon_password, default port 27015; Palworld `PalWorldSettings.ini` OptionSettings → RCONEnabled/AdminPassword/RCONPort). Port passes through `parsePort` (returns the **parsed integer 1–65535 or a safe default**, never the raw text). Password is used **only as an RCON packet body** — never a shell/argv token — so it cannot inject; length-bounded and never surfaced in an error.
- **Command box** validated (`validateRconCommand`): non-empty, ≤512 chars, rejects NUL/newline/control chars (would forge extra RCON frames).
- **Player ids** allowlisted `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$` before templating into a kick/ban verb.
- **Shell**: family/unit/family-hint strings are compile-time constants; every located path re-validated against an absolute-path allowlist (`isSafeRemotePath`, no `..`/`//`) and single-quoted (`shq`); backup tar interpolates only allowlisted, quoted paths. No customer string is ever concatenated raw into a shell command.
- `safeError` collapses unexpected errors so root/RCON credentials or internals never reach the customer.

### Per-game RCON coverage (of the 6)
- **Source RCON wired**: Minecraft, CS2, Palworld.
- **Rust**: RCON is WebSocket (`rcon.web`) — different protocol, **deferred** (power/logs/schedules/backups fully work; console box disabled with a note).
- **Valheim, Terraria**: no native remote console — command box disabled with a note; power/logs/schedules/backups work.

- Rust WebSocket RCON.
- One-click mod/plugin install (not started; direct mod upload possible today via the existing Files tab).

- Requires `prisma generate` + a migration for `GameSchedule` and the two new `JobType` values before the code type-checks/runs (I did not run prisma/build per instructions).
- The worker's real SSH paths run when not in SANDBOX; RCON/power/backup only act while the VM is RUNNING.
